title: Nasal spray live attenuated influenza vaccine: the first experience in Italy in children and adolescents during the 2020-21 season.
ehr_evidence: A questionnaire was given out to parents on the day of the vaccination, on a voluntary and anonymous basis, through which information about children and their parents was collected... Between one and 3 months later, the parents were contacted by phone to check if there had been any adverse reactions following (Fluenz Tetra™) administration.
summary: An observational survey study of the quadrivalent live attenuated influenza vaccine (qLAIV/Fluenz Tetra) administered to 3,226 children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in Milan, Italy during the 2020-21 season, assessing adverse events, parental satisfaction, and intention to repeat vaccination.
key_findings: Adverse events were reported in 24.8% of children (80.6% mild, 18.1% moderate, 1.3% significant); the most common were rhinitis/cold (52.5%) and fever (24.4%).
Children aged 2-5 years had an increased risk of adverse events compared with 6-10 years (aRR 1.7, 95% CI 1.5-1.9, p<0.001) and 11-17 years (aRR 1.5, 95% CI 1-2.2, p=0.051).
Children with at least one acute infectious disease in 2020 had higher risk (aRR 1.2, 95% CI 1.1-1.4, p=0.004) and those with a chronic disease had higher risk (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2-2.1, p=0.001).
Males had a decreased probability of adverse reactions compared with females (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.8-1, p=0.011); prematurity was not associated with adverse events (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.7-1.1, p=0.220).
83.3% of parents were very satisfied and 83.8% intended to re-vaccinate their children with qLAIV the following year.
Adverse reactions were the main factor influencing the decision not to repeat vaccination (aRR 5.5, 95% CI 2.4-12.5, p<0.001).
captured_features: Child gender, date and place of birth, gestational age, siblings, daycare attendance
Parent age, place of birth, level of education, chronic diseases, prior flu vaccination
Acute infectious diseases in 2020 prior to vaccination
Parental satisfaction and intention to repeat vaccination
Health worker satisfaction and willingness to repeat
pathologies_diseases: Adverse events/reactions following qLAIV vaccination (rhinitis, fever, malaise)
Allergic diseases, pulmonary diseases, and other chronic conditions studied as factors
study_design: Observational cross-sectional survey with telephone follow-up
population: 3,226 children and adolescents aged 2-17 years (59.8% preschoolers, 36.6% primary school-age, 3.6% adolescents) from 2,152 families in Milan, Italy, 2020-21 influenza season
exposure_domain: Vaccination (quadrivalent live attenuated influenza vaccine, qLAIV/Fluenz Tetra)
limitations: Self-reported, questionnaire-based data subject to recall and reporting bias.
Low follow-up response rate (2,152 of 3,571 selected families responded).
Selection bias: population over-represented by highly educated parents and did not reach all social sections.
Anonymous and voluntary participation may limit generalizability.
